blocks.content: The pattern of flow of water through well-defined channels is known as drainage, and the network of such channels is called a drainage system.

rows: Outward from a central high peak or dome
Inward towards a central basin or lake
Volcanic cones, elevated domes, mountain peaks
Rivers originating from Amarkantak Hills (Narmada, Son)

items: Amarkantak Plateau is a frequently asked example of radial drainage, giving origin to rivers like the Narmada and Son.
Identify the difference between Antecedent rivers (Indus, Sutlej, Brahmaputra) which predated Himalayan uplift and Superimposed rivers (Damodar, Subarnarekha).
Loktak Lake in Manipur and Sambhar Lake in Rajasthan are classic examples of centripetal drainage patterns tested in Indian competitive exams.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: A dendritic drainage pattern resembles the branches of a tree and develops in areas with uniform rock structure like the Northern Plains.
Trellis pattern forms where primary tributaries flow parallel to each other and secondary tributaries join them at right angles along soft rock strata.
Radial drainage patterns originate from a central high elevation, with rivers flowing outward in all directions like spokes of a wheel.
Centripetal drainage occurs when streams converge from surrounding high grounds into a central depression, lake, or basin.
